climbing_route.label: Short step above the pass
climbing_route.notes: From the base of Inner Constance's northeast side, a short step just above the pass leads into the rising traverse.

climbing_route.label: Rising traverse on the north ridge/crest
climbing_route.notes: A rising traverse along the right side of the north ridge/crest on broken, blocky terrain, with occasional class 4 (and low 5th class) moves where the crest steepens, working up to the summit.

climbing_route.label: White Chuck Glacier to the White River Glacier
climbing_route.notes: From camp, climb to Foam Pass and cross the White Chuck Glacier and Glacier Gap onto the White River Glacier. This is glacier travel, and rope/crampons/axe are standard gear here; crevasses are typically open and visible to weave around by late summer but can be harder to read under early-season snow bridges.

climbing_route.label: Connecting ridge NNW to the 7,400 ft saddle
climbing_route.notes: From the glacier, gain the flat shoulder at ~6,000 ft, then climb the connecting ridge NNW to a bulge at 7,200 ft, cross a small basin below Kololo's east summit, and continue west a quarter mile to a saddle at 7,400 ft.

climbing_route.label: Cirque-edge ridge and summit scramble
climbing_route.notes: From the saddle the ridge forming the east edge of the White River Glacier cirque leads to the final glacier/talus/ledge scramble to the summit.

climbing_route.label: South ridge from Lizard Col
climbing_route.notes: From the col the South Route gains Lizard Mountain's south ridge directly to the summit, a straightforward but loose scramble of roughly 600 vertical feet; stay near the crest to avoid the worst rubble on the flanks.

climbing_route.label: South slopes and gullies from Azurite Pass
climbing_route.notes: From Azurite Pass (6,680+ ft), leave the trail and scramble northeast/east up Ballard's broad south-facing slopes and gullies, watching for the correct gully to the true summit block.

climbing_route.label: Summit block from the west/southwest shoulder
climbing_route.notes: The final several hundred feet to the 6,836 ft summit are scrambling on broken shale and loose scree, from the shoulder immediately west/southwest of Claywood's summit block.

climbing_route.label: East ridge to the saddle
climbing_route.notes: Gain the ridge and follow moderate slopes of sand, scree and talus - loose in spots, with real route-finding required - up to the saddle between the true summit and a lower false summit (roughly 7,200-7,600 ft). Snow can linger on the upper ridge well into early summer; carry an ice axe and know how to use it before the passes fully melt out.

climbing_route.label: Summit scramble from the saddle
climbing_route.notes: From the saddle, several hundred feet of enjoyable scrambling over blocky rock leads to the summit at 8,097 ft; some parties note a notch below the true summit block that's crossed before a short, shallow summit gully.

climbing_route.label: Hinman/Foss Glacier basin from La Bohn Gap
climbing_route.notes: From La Bohn Gap the route continues north onto what remains of the Hinman/Foss Glacier basin - now much diminished and largely bare rock/permanent snowfield rather than a true crevassed glacier in most recent seasons, but still worth crampons/axe and glacier-travel judgment in early season or after a big snow year. Potential crevasse/bergschrund hazard on the lingering glacier remnant, mostly early-season.

climbing_route.label: Summit ridge to the true summit
climbing_route.notes: Ridge/scree scrambling to the summit ridge and along it about half a mile to the true summit (7,492 ft). Loose rock on the final scramble.

climbing_route.label: Talus and heather to the southwest ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the west basin, climb talus and heather to gain the southwest ridge, passing below a distinctive band of white rock.

climbing_route.label: Summit gully
climbing_route.notes: The route narrows into an exposed gully near the summit.

climbing_route.label: Stacked boulders to the summit block
climbing_route.notes: Finish over stacked boulders to the summit block.
